title: Centuries of rebuilding made a mound at Bahrain's ancient port
body: Qal'at al-Bahrain was a harbour and capital of the Dilmun civilisation. Buildings and other remains from successive settlements accumulated at the site, creating an artificial mound archaeologists call a tell.
takeaway: An excavation can read the mound vertically, with different levels preserving different periods of the same port.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Qal'at al-Bahrain (2005)
visual: an archaeological trench showing stacked layers beside ancient stone walls
